title: Michigan required provisions and property-casualty laws
summary: One wild week at Dana's agency: Michigan's fire policy rules, appraisal, notice periods, the Essential Insurance Act, TRIA and the guaranty association.
objectives: Recall the minimums and deadlines every Michigan fire policy must include
Walk through Michigan appraisal and home insurance termination notice rules
Apply Essential Insurance Act eligibility; know its underwriting and declination rules
Know what a dropped producer may do, and the TRIA and guaranty association numbers

scenes.title: Dana's wild week of Michigan insurance laws
scenes.subtitle: Exam Basics: fire policies, appraisal, notices, the Essential Insurance Act, TRIA, the guaranty association

beats.text: June in Grand Rapids. Lightning hits the Millers' roof, and their kitchen catches fire. Everyone gets out safe.
beats.say: June in Grand Rapids. Lightning hits the Millers' roof, and their kitchen catches fire. Everyone gets out safe.

beats.text: Sam's calling. Long week ahead.
beats.say: Sam's calling. Long week ahead.

scenes.title: Monday: the floor under every fire policy

draw.text: Floor: ACV at the time of loss, for fire and lightning
Starts 12:01 a.m. standard time, at the property
Insurer cancels: at least 10 days' notice (home: see the Act)
Minimum earned premium: pro rata or $25, whichever is greater

beats.text: Monday. That fire came from lightning. In Michigan, every fire policy must cover at least fire and lightning, at actual cash value at the time of loss.
beats.say: Monday. That fire came from lightning. In Michigan, every fire policy must cover at least fire and lightning, at actual cash value at the time of loss.

beats.text: A floor, not a ceiling: policies may pay more. Coverage starts at 12:01 a.m. standard time, where the property is.
beats.say: A floor, not a ceiling: policies may pay more. Coverage starts at twelve oh one A M standard time, where the property is.

beats.text: The insured may cancel any time. The insurer needs at least 10 days' written notice, but home insurance has its own rules.
beats.say: The insured may cancel any time. The insurer needs at least ten days' written notice, but home insurance has its own rules.

beats.text: Whoever cancels, the minimum earned premium is the greater of pro rata or $25.
beats.say: Whoever cancels, the minimum earned premium is the greater of pro rata or twenty-five dollars.

beats.text: The policy must state what suspends coverage, but a vacancy suspension isn't required.
beats.say: The policy must state what suspends coverage, but a vacancy suspension isn't required.

scenes.title: Required in every Michigan fire policy?

items.text: At least actual cash value at the time of loss
items.why: ACV at the time of loss is the legal minimum.

items.text: Coverage starts at 12:01 a.m. standard time
items.why: It takes effect at 12:01 a.m. where the property is.
A policy may pay it, but ACV is the minimum. One way to figure ACV: replacement cost minus depreciation.

items.text: Covers direct loss by fire and lightning
items.why: Fire and lightning are the minimum perils.

items.text: Coverage stops after 30 days of vacancy
items.why: The law requires no vacancy suspension.

items.text: Min. earned premium: greater of pro rata or $25
items.why: Whoever cancels. Pro rata under $25? The insurer keeps $25.

beats.text: Your turn: required by law, or not?
beats.say: Your turn: required by law, or not?

reveal.text: Replacement cost and a vacancy suspension aren't required. The rest are.
reveal.say: Replacement cost and a vacancy suspension aren't required. The rest are.

scenes.title: Tuesday: what's the kitchen worth?
scenes.src: MCL 500.2833(1)(m); memory hook mn_prop-04; question prop-011
scenes.plain: A way to settle a fight over how much a loss is worth: each side picks an appraiser, and an umpire breaks a deadlock.
scenes.example: The adjuster says the Millers' kitchen loss is $18,000. Sam's contractor says $30,000. Sam sends the insurer a written demand for appraisal.
scenes.exam: Written demand by either side. 20 days: each names an independent appraiser. 15 days: agree on an umpire, or a circuit judge in the county picks.

beats.text: Tuesday. The adjuster says the kitchen loss is $18,000.
beats.say: Tuesday. The adjuster says the kitchen loss is eighteen thousand dollars.

beats.text: My contractor says $30,000!
beats.say: My contractor says thirty thousand dollars!

beats.text: In Michigan, if the sides disagree on actual cash value or the amount of loss, either can demand appraisal in writing.
beats.say: In Michigan, if the sides disagree on actual cash value or the amount of loss, either can demand appraisal in writing.

beats.text: Within 20 days of the demand, each names a competent, independent appraiser.
beats.say: Within twenty days of the demand, each names a competent, independent appraiser.

beats.text: Then 15 days to agree on an umpire. Stuck? A circuit judge in the county picks. Don't flip 20 and 15.
beats.say: Then fifteen days to agree on an umpire. Stuck? A circuit judge in the county picks. Don't flip twenty and fifteen.

scenes.title: Flash-forward: the umpire standoff
scenes.src: MCL 500.2833(1)(m); questions prop-011, prop-012; memory hook mn_prop-04

beats.text: Both appraisers are named. Fifteen days later, still no agreed umpire. What should Sam do?
beats.say: Both appraisers are named. Fifteen days later, still no agreed umpire. What should Sam do?

options.label: Let the insurer's appraiser pick alone
options.fail: The umpire must be impartial: the two appraisers pick together. Stuck for 15 days? Either side may ask a circuit court judge.

beats.text: The insurer's appraiser picks his own umpire. Sam cries foul.
beats.say: The insurer's appraiser picks his own umpire. Sam cries foul.

options.label: Ask the state insurance Director to pick
options.fail: Michigan law sends this to a circuit court judge in the county where the loss occurred or the property is located.

beats.text: Sam waits at the state insurance office. Wrong desk.
beats.say: Sam waits at the state insurance office. Wrong desk.

options.label: Ask a circuit court judge in the county
options.win: Michigan law: stuck for 15 days? Either side may ask a circuit court judge in the county of the loss or the property to pick the umpire.

beats.text: The judge picks an impartial umpire.
beats.say: The judge picks an impartial umpire.

reveal.text: The umpire and Sam's appraiser agree: $24,000. Any 2 of the 3 set the loss in writing.
reveal.say: The umpire and Sam's appraiser agree: twenty-four thousand dollars. Any two of the three set the loss in writing.

reveal.text: Each side pays its own appraiser; the umpire and other costs are split equally.
reveal.say: Each side pays its own appraiser; the umpire and other costs are split equally.

scenes.title: Two Michigan clocks: sue and pay
scenes.src: MCL 500.2833(1)(p),(q); MCL 500.2845; memory hook mn_prop-03; questions prop-008, prop-009
scenes.plain: Paused. A deadline clock that stops running for a while.
scenes.example: Like pausing a game clock: from the day you report a loss until the insurer formally denies liability, your time to sue doesn't run.
scenes.exam: Sue within 1 year after the loss or the policy's longer period, tolled from notice of loss until formal denial.

draw.text: Sue: 1 year, or the policy's longer period
Except: in some towns, part of a big fire payment is held back

beats.text: How long do we have to sue them?
beats.say: How long do we have to sue them?

beats.text: In Michigan, 1 year after the loss, or the policy's longer period. And that clock can be tolled.
beats.say: In Michigan, one year after the loss, or the policy's longer period. And that clock can be tolled.

beats.text: Tolled means paused: from the day the loss is reported until the insurer formally denies liability.
beats.say: Tolled means paused: from the day the loss is reported until the insurer formally denies liability.

beats.text: The loss is payable within 30 days after proof of the amount of loss, unless the fire-loss withholding law applies.
beats.say: The loss is payable within thirty days after proof of the amount of loss, unless the fire-loss withholding law applies.

scenes.title: Wednesday: the Essential Insurance Act
scenes.plain: For home and auto insurance: the insurer refusing to keep insuring you, for any reason other than nonpayment.
scenes.example: The Millers' neighbor always pays on time, but his insurer won't renew his home policy. That's a termination.
scenes.exam: At least 30 days' written notice, with the effective date and each specific reason. First 55 days: 20 days. Nonpayment: as the policy says.

beats.text: Wednesday. The Millers' neighbor always pays, but his insurer won't renew. Under Michigan's Essential Insurance Act, that's a termination.
beats.say: Wednesday. The Millers' neighbor always pays, but his insurer won't renew. Under Michigan's Essential Insurance Act, that's a termination.

beats.text: Picture a Michigan road sign: at least 30 days' written notice, with the effective date and each specific reason.
beats.say: Picture a Michigan road sign: at least thirty days' written notice, with the effective date and each specific reason.

beats.text: First 55 days of a new policy? 20 days after mailing. Nonpayment? As the policy says.
beats.say: First fifty-five days of a new policy? Twenty days after mailing. Nonpayment? As the policy says.

scenes.title: The underwriter's call: Jen's grandma's policy

beats.text: Jen's grandma lives in her own house. Her new homeowners policy is 40 days old.
beats.say: Jen's grandma lives in her own house. Her new homeowners policy is forty days old.

beats.text: Her insurer wants out, not for nonpayment. What's the fastest the Act allows?
beats.say: Her insurer wants out, not for nonpayment. What's the fastest the Act allows?

options.label: Phone her: coverage ends today
options.fail: A termination isn't effective without written notice mailed or delivered first. In the first 55 days: at least 20 days after mailing.

beats.text: A quick phone call. Nothing ends.
beats.say: A quick phone call. Nothing ends.

options.label: Mail a notice: coverage ends in 10 days
options.fail: 10 days is the fire policy and general casualty minimum. For home insurance, the Essential Insurance Act controls: 20 days here.

beats.text: Too fast. Ten days is the fire policy rule.
beats.say: Too fast. Ten days is the fire policy rule.

options.label: Mail a notice: ends 20 days after mailing
options.win: Under the Act, a notice mailed within the first 55 days after a policy is first issued can take effect 20 days after mailing. A policy may give more.

beats.text: Day 40 is inside the first 55 days: 20 days after mailing works.
beats.say: Day forty is inside the first fifty-five days: twenty days after mailing works.

options.label: Mail a notice: ends 30 days after mailing
options.fail: Allowed, but not the fastest. 30 days is the usual rule; a notice mailed in the first 55 days can take effect 20 days after mailing.

beats.text: Ten extra days of coverage. Legal, but twenty was allowed.
beats.say: Ten extra days of coverage. Legal, but twenty was allowed.

reveal.text: Mailed after day 55? Back to 30. Michigan's general casualty minimum is 10 days; a malpractice nonrenewal needs at least 60.
reveal.say: Mailed after day fifty-five? Back to thirty. Michigan's general casualty minimum is ten days; a malpractice nonrenewal needs at least sixty.

scenes.title: Thursday: who is an eligible person?
scenes.src: MCL 500.2103(2), 500.2117(1), 500.2119; question prop-020; memory hook mn_prop-06
scenes.plain: Someone an insurer may refuse, not renew or limit only under written rules the Act allows. You live there, as owner or tenant (owners: 4 units max).
scenes.example: Ana owns a 3-unit building in Lansing and lives upstairs: eligible. Ben owns a rental house in Saginaw but lives elsewhere: not eligible.
scenes.exam: Knocked out, for example: an arson conviction within 5 years, or property taxes delinquent 2 or more years.

draw.text: Arson conviction within 5 years, or taxes 2 or more years late

beats.text: Thursday. An insurer may refuse, not renew or limit an eligible person's home insurance only under written rules the Act allows.
beats.say: Thursday. An insurer may refuse, not renew or limit an eligible person's home insurance only under written rules the Act allows.

beats.text: You live there, as owner or tenant. Own up to 4 units and live in one? Eligible. A landlord living elsewhere? Not eligible.
beats.say: You live there, as owner or tenant. Own up to four units and live in one? Eligible. A landlord living elsewhere? Not eligible.

beats.text: Knockouts include an arson conviction within 5 years, or property taxes 2 or more years delinquent.
beats.say: Knockouts include an arson conviction within five years, or property taxes two or more years delinquent.

scenes.title: Eligible person, or not?
scenes.src: MCL 500.2103(2); question prop-020; memory hook mn_prop-06

cards.text: Rosa rents an apartment in Lansing and lives there.
cards.why: A tenant of an apartment is an eligible person for home insurance.

cards.text: Tony's cousin owns a 2-unit building in Flint and rents out both units. He lives across town.
cards.why: Up to 4 units counts only if the owner lives there. A non-occupying owner is not an eligible person.

cards.text: Tony owns a 4-unit apartment building in Detroit and lives in one of the units.
cards.why: The owner-occupant of a dwelling of up to 4 units is an eligible person.

cards.text: A homeowner was convicted of arson 2 years ago.
cards.why: An arson conviction within the preceding 5 years makes a person ineligible.

cards.text: A homeowner's property taxes have been delinquent for 3 years.
cards.why: Property taxes delinquent 2 or more years make a person ineligible.

beats.text: Your turn: eligible person, or not?
beats.say: Your turn: eligible person, or not?

reveal.text: Live there, and if you own the building, 4 units max. Then check the knockouts.
reveal.say: Live there, and if you own the building, four units max. Then check the knockouts.

scenes.title: The Act: no redlining
scenes.plain: Under Michigan's Essential Insurance Act: refusing, not renewing or limiting home or auto coverage because of where the risk is located.
scenes.example: An insurer turns down every home applicant in one Grand Rapids neighborhood, whatever shape each house is in. That's redlining.
scenes.exam: Watch out: age of the dwelling is the classic EXCEPT answer. The 90 days is the applicant's window to ask, not the insurer's deadline.

beats.text: For home underwriting under Michigan's Essential Insurance Act: judge the house's condition, never its birthday or its location.
beats.say: For home underwriting under Michigan's Essential Insurance Act: judge the house's condition, never its birthday or its location.

beats.text: Refusing or limiting home coverage because of the risk's location is redlining, and the Act prohibits it. Outside the Act, Michigan lets property insurers use location only with a statistically significant fire-loss link in its ZIP code.
beats.say: Refusing or limiting home coverage because of the risk's location is redlining, and the Act prohibits it. Outside the Act, Michigan lets property insurers use location only with a statistically significant fire-loss link in its zip code.

beats.text: Saying no? Give each specific reason. Applied out loud? Within 90 days, they can ask for a written explanation.
beats.say: Saying no? Give each specific reason. Applied out loud? Within ninety days, they can ask for a written explanation.

scenes.title: Friday: Tony's terrorism coverage
scenes.src: TRIA §§102(1),(7), 103(b),(c),(e), 108(a), 15 U.S.C. 6701 note (current law as of Oct 2026); memory hook mn_prop-08

draw.text: TRIA created the federal Terrorism Risk Insurance Program
losses must top this; then the Treasury Secretary certifies
insurer's deductible: 20% of last year's premium
Uncle Sam's share above the deductible
industry losses before any federal payment
Ends Dec 31, 2027 under current law: recheck

beats.text: Terrorism coverage on my renewal? I make pizza!
beats.say: Terrorism coverage on my renewal? I make pizza!

beats.text: A federal law, TRIA, makes insurers offer it. Picture Uncle Sam's terror ladder.
beats.say: A federal law, T R I A, makes insurers offer it. Picture Uncle Sam's terror ladder.

beats.text: First rung: the Treasury Secretary certifies an act of terrorism, consulting the Homeland Security Secretary and the Attorney General. Losses must top $5 million.
beats.say: First rung: the Treasury Secretary certifies an act of terrorism, consulting the Homeland Security Secretary and the Attorney General. Losses must top five million dollars.

beats.text: Next, each insurer's deductible: 20% of its prior-year direct earned premium. Above it, Uncle Sam pays 80%.
beats.say: Next, each insurer's deductible: twenty percent of its prior-year direct earned premium. Above it, Uncle Sam pays eighty percent.

beats.text: No federal payment until industry losses top $200 million; the annual cap is $100 billion. Don't swap 20 and 80!
beats.say: No federal payment until industry losses top two hundred million dollars; the annual cap is one hundred billion dollars. Don't swap twenty and eighty!

beats.text: Under current law it ends December 31, 2027, but extension bills were pending in 2026: recheck.
beats.say: Under current law it ends December thirty-first, twenty twenty-seven, but extension bills were pending in twenty twenty-six: recheck.

draw.text: Monday: the Millers' renewal is due

beats.text: Saturday. Dana sent the Millers' insurer only 18 home and auto applications in 12 months. It ends her agency contract.
beats.say: Saturday. Dana sent the Millers' insurer only eighteen home and auto applications in twelve months. It ends her agency contract.

beats.text: The contract is silent on what comes next. Dana is an independent producer. What now?
beats.say: The contract is silent on what comes next. Dana is an independent producer. What now?

options.label: Renew the Millers once, on her own
options.fail: Michigan law: with a silent agreement, a terminated producer may not renew, bind new risks or increase the insurer's obligation without approval.

beats.text: Dana renews the Millers herself. Not without the insurer's approval!
beats.say: Dana renews the Millers herself. Not without the insurer's approval!

options.label: Tell the Millers their policy is canceled
options.fail: Michigan law: an insurer may not cancel or nonrenew a policy because the producer's contract was terminated.

beats.text: Jen panics. But the insurer can't cancel because Dana's contract ended.
beats.say: Jen panics. But the insurer can't cancel because Dana's contract ended.

options.label: Service policies; ask to bind or renew
options.win: Michigan law: she may service existing policies, but not bind, renew or increase the insurer's obligation without approval.

beats.text: Dana keeps servicing, and asks before renewing.
beats.say: Dana keeps servicing, and asks before renewing.

beats.text: And dropping her for under 25 applications in 12 months? Allowed.
beats.say: And dropping her for under twenty-five applications in twelve months? Allowed.

draw.text: An insurer may drop a home and auto producer only for:
Malfeasance. Breach of fiduciary duty or trust. Code violation. Failure to perform.
Or under 25 home and auto apps in 12 months

reveal.text: In Michigan, a home and auto insurer may drop an independent producer only for listed reasons.
reveal.say: In Michigan, a home and auto insurer may drop an independent producer only for listed reasons.

reveal.text: Malfeasance is another. But never mainly for the agency's location, or losses tied to it.
reveal.say: Malfeasance is another. But never mainly for the agency's location, or losses tied to it.

scenes.title: Sunday: when an insurer goes broke
scenes.src: MCL 500.7911, 500.7925(2),(4),(6), 500.7931(4); base amounts, CPI-adjusted; memory hook mn_prop-01

spots.label: The lifeboat
spots.text: When a member insurer is insolvent, the Michigan Property and Casualty Guaranty Association pays its covered claims.

spots.label: No license, no lifeboat
spots.text: Insurers authorized in Michigan for lines other than life or disability belong. A surplus lines insurer is not treated as authorized: no membership, no protection.

spots.label: Unearned premium
spots.text: Refunds of unearned premium the broke insurer owes: covered up to the first $500 per person (base amount, adjusted each year). No refund under $50.

spots.label: Claim cap
spots.text: The part of a claim over $5 million (base amount) isn't covered. Workers' comp and no-fault PIP claims aren't capped.

spots.label: Net-worth limit
spots.text: No claims by or against an insured whose net worth tops $25 million (base amount).

spots.label: A 30-day ride
spots.text: In-force policies continue until they expire, are replaced or canceled, but no more than 30 days after the receiver is appointed.

beats.text: Sunday's news: an insurer is insolvent. Its covered claims go to the Michigan Property and Casualty Guaranty Association.
beats.say: Sunday's news: an insurer is insolvent. Its covered claims go to the Michigan Property and Casualty Guaranty Association.

beats.text: Picture a lifeboat. No license, no lifeboat. Tap the glowing spots.
beats.say: Picture a lifeboat. No license, no lifeboat. Tap the glowing spots.

reveal.text: The lifeboat runs on fives. Refunds: $50 up to $500. Claim cap: $5 million. Net-worth limit: $25 million. Plus a 30-day ride.
reveal.say: The lifeboat runs on fives. Refunds: fifty dollars up to five hundred dollars. Claim cap: five million dollars. Net-worth limit: twenty-five million dollars. Plus a thirty-day ride.

reveal.text: The dollar maximums are inflation-adjusted bases; exam items may use base or current figures.
reveal.say: The dollar maximums are inflation-adjusted bases; exam items may use base or current figures.

scenes.q: Which claim is NOT subject to Michigan's $5 million guaranty claim cap (statutory base)?
scenes.why: The per-claim cap does not apply to workers' compensation claims or no-fault PIP claims.

beats.text: Which claim escapes the cap?
beats.say: Which claim escapes the cap?

reveal.text: The no-fault PIP claim. PIP and workers' comp aren't capped.
reveal.say: The no-fault P I P claim. P I P and workers' comp aren't capped.

items: Fire policy: ACV, fire, lightning, 12:01 a.m., $25 min. earned premium
Pay: 30 days after proof. Sue: at least 1 yr, tolled. Appraisal: 20/15
Home termination: 30 days' notice, or 20 in the first 55 days
Act: live there (owners: 4 units max); condition, not age or location
TRIA 20% deductible, feds 80%; guaranty cap spares PIP, workers' comp

beats.text: What a week! Dana kept servicing her policies. Weeks later, Sam's appraisal wrapped up.
beats.say: What a week! Dana kept servicing her policies. Weeks later, Sam's appraisal wrapped up.

beats.say: Next week, my phone goes in a drawer.
